nodes.question: What is being scrutinized in response to the environmental crisis within democratic governance?
nodes.answer: The routines and institutions of democratic governance, as well as their methods of intermediating between institutional politics and the people, are being scrutinized.
nodes.paragraph: Whilethe impact of these forms of con ict management, bridge- building, or even cooperation may vary, they altogether de ne the nature of local interactive governance and itscapacities for promoting sustainable development and democracy. Keywords Interactive governance /C1Local climate governance /C1Civil society /C1 Local administration /C1 Collaboration Introduction While environmental challenges are high on the publicagenda, they have raised many questions concerning the ability of society and politics to cope with them. Much ofthe attention goes either to government action or to the various forms of people S reaction, namely protest on the streets and at the voting ballots. Especially liberaldemocracies, claiming to bridge people S will and institu- tional politics, get distressed by the massive challenges of the environmental crisis. The respective routines andinstitutions of democratic governance, as well as their methods of intermediating between institutional politics and the people, are being subjected to scrutiny. There is asearch for more interactive forms and proceedings that can mitigate con ict and dissent and facilitate the creation of legitimate and ef cient environmental politics. This calls for a relational approach (Evers & von Essen, 2019 & 2024 ), that takes up the roles of civic engagement and civil society actors as part of a wider complex interplay between state (political and administrative institutions), civil soci- ety, and economy.
